quest.title: Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved
quest.description: Finally, you reach Nantianmen. A curious ancient tree has quietly stood here throughout the ages, bearing witness to all that has come to pass. To rescue the miners and solve this puzzle once and for all, you proceed to the ancient site that holds all the answers...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Gold x5, Dream Solvent x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kun Jun! We need to get going!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: No problem! I'm done here.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Any results, Mr. Kun Jun?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: There are many beautiful rocks here, but nothing out of the ordinary. I couldn't find any clues.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Then again, the memories of ore can shift with the passage of time and the changing of the environment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there a pattern to it?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Hmm, difficult to say... I feel that ore memories tend to be from the recent past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So there's never any ancient memories?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Rocks endure, but as eons pass their memories are erased. Those memories that survive are rooted in powerful emotion or thought.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes sense — it is the same for people!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Indeed... Let's keep going.

talks.objective: Head to the ancient tree and investigate

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Wow, such an immense tree!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there's so many mysterious-looking crystals up there too... amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This ancient tree...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Let's conduct separate investigations. I'll take that area, perhaps you could survey this section.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Alright then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kun Jun, can you see anything worth investigating?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Well... there is this stone tablet here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Doesn't seem very interesting... Paimon's gonna look over there.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Huh? It's worth a try, surely. Let me see...

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: (This is...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! What's wrong?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: ...Just a bit light-headed... It's passed, nothing to worry about.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you see anything?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Not... hmm... not yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #*sigh* Whatever, Paimon's going to investigate over there. Why don't you climb the tree and have a look, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're sure there'll be clues in the tree?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you don't try you don't know! Anyway, you'll be able to get a good look at our surroundings from up there!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Oh! Uh... you think so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When has Paimon ever come up with a bad idea, hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute... Paimon can fly! *sigh* Alright, Paimon will go, you wait here, Paimon will—

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: All of you, come here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Zhongli's voice came from... behind the tree. Did he find another clue?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick, let's go see! Maybe he found another miner!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This has been newly dug. It would appear our answer is up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that a voice coming from the tunnel? Eek! Someone else go first!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Compose yourselves. I will lead us in.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: There is an unusual presence emanating from inside the tunnel. Prepare yourselves, and tread lightly.

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: Ugh... ugh...

talks.objective: Enter the Domain at the end of the underground tunnel
Learn the truth of the situation

dialogues.speaker: Jiu
dialogues.text: Morax! A thousand years after you sealed me underground... you return for the second time...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You should call it by its name, Azhdaha... fate.

dialogues.speaker: Jiu
dialogues.text: Fate?

dialogues.speaker: Jiu
dialogues.text: Fate!!! Hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Jiu
dialogues.text: So here lies the wisdom of the gods? Destroy all deemed redundant, enlist tyrants to ravage the wilderness!
No. You have forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That... that voice...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Azhdaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Kun Jun!?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Morax. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Jiu
dialogues.text: Y—You're...

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun?
dialogues.text: Azhdaha... the very same.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: During the battle... you embued us with your power...

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun?
dialogues.text: Haha... yes. It was all I could manage.

choices.text: Then... which one is the real Azhdaha?

response.speaker: Kun Jun?
response.text: Forgive me for concealing the truth, Traveler. There were things that only became clear to me upon reaching this tree.

response.speaker: Kun Jun?
response.text: Allow me to elaborate. I am not Azhdaha the whole... but a fragment.

response.speaker: Kun Jun?
response.text: Heaven and earth, yin and yang, opposing forces... You can consider the existence of me and the Azhdaha you see there, to be a reflection of such polarities. "We" are a schism of the will... the will of Azhdaha.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... so there are two Azhdahas!?

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: No! It can't be! That's impossible...!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: When the seal loosened, your power manifested in this world as a child. With this new identity, you were able to vent about the forces that suppressed you... but would anyone listen... would they even care?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: That's when it occurred to you. The loosening of the seal constituted an opportunity to strike back. Kidnapping the miners was all in aid of digging to the entrance to the seal itself. Your plan was to launch an attack on both ends. From outside... and within. Thereby fully destroying the seal.

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: The audacity! Are you insane!? If you truly are a part of me, how is it you find yourself standing on the side of the betrayer!?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I was another power awakened with the loosening of the seal. Too weak to reincarnate, but strong enough to possess a human body.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I was barely conscious... I couldn't remember who I was. Only the past would elicit a reaction from me... But my aim was clear: Find Morax... and aid him in stopping you.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I had sensed that something was amiss when you mentioned Dragonfall. Had your power been but a little stronger, I would've recognized you.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Don't blame yourself, I have changed beyond all recognition. Only when I touched the stone tablet... did I truly remember.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: It's been so long. A secret beyond all comprehension, of youthful humanity and ancient dragon-kind... Morax, do you want to tell the tale?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: There would be no harm in it. The decision is yours.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Haha, you haven't changed. Then allow me.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Azhdaha was once a friend and ally of the Geo Archon, Morax, with a lifespan far exceeding that of mankind. However, that which is derived of the earth is no more or less than the earth itself...

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: The memories of rocks do not last long. Those memories that survive are rooted in powerful emotion. But as time passes, so these memories fade into obscurity. Erosion is the world's greatest destroyer of memories.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Erosion...?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Erosion ground Azhdaha's consciousness into oblivion. Slowly, he forgot the face of his old friend, and his memories of defending Liyue Harbor disintegrated.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Azhdaha, now incomplete, became irascible... aggressive.

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: What would you expect!? It was humanity that attacked the Ley Lines that sustained me!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: This much is true. Which is why "you" attacked The Chasm... why "you" waged war against Morax.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: In the beginning, in order to open up new territory and increase production, the citizens of Liyue came to the mountains to mine. Overexploitation caused the Ley Lines to quake, which brought untold suffering to "us."

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Erosion made "us" even more savage. No matter how we struggled, we lost the ability to coexist with humanity... we lost all reason.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Morax shared with us some of his power, to prevent further erosion. But... it was futile. Everything returns to dust. It is the natural order, an unstoppable force.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: And so, "we" became "you." And from your will... "I" emerged.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I am your final contract. Witness the promise between Azhdaha and Morax. You can hate me... but you cannot deny me.

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: No... no...

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I am the remnants of Azhdaha's benevolence, the echo of a contract set in stone. I harbor a willingness to go further, a willingness to coexist peacefully with mankind.

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: No, no! It is I, Azhdaha, forged of elemental crystal, bearer of the weight and memories of the earth, older than the mountains and the oceans that decides! I will not swear allegiance to this insect!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Morax is not an insect.

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: A lord over insects is nothing but an insect in turn!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: You forgot yourself. Nobody held Morax in higher regard than you or I.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: That which you have forgotten, I hold here in my heart. If you are the memory of the earth... then I am the memory of coexistence... of coexistence with humanity.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: All powers under heaven, rise and fall of land and sea...

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: ...A star appears within the wild... a sun ascends as bright as... jade...

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: Strange... What... what is this feeling? And all this...

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: You are spent, and I will soon disappear. Before I do, heed these words.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: In the wilderness, snow falls on a spring day. In an instant it will melt. Even where it is fleeting and leaves no trace. Even where it will never fall again...

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: No, that isn't true! I don't accept this as fate!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Perhaps it isn't. But it remains... an inevitable misfortune.

response.speaker: Jiu
response.text: Mor... ax...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The little girl vanished...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Are you satisfied, Azhdaha?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I had to make amends. Satisfaction had no part in it.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: So, Morax... you call yourself Zhongli these days?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I do.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Well, I'm afraid old habits die hard. To me, you're Morax.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: As you please.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I never did forget your gift of sight.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I hardly lifted a finger. Think nothing of it.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: And yet you could see. You wouldn't know the yearning of a blind dragon, searching for the sun. A pair of eyes, from Morax to Azhdaha. This... I will remember this.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Your power is nearly spent.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: ...Perceptive as always, my friend.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Shall we get going, you and I?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Surely the pressing matter is still that of the miners trapped outside the seal?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed. Hence the need to get going, to fix the damage left in your wake.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Ha... straight down to business, as always. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: Ugh... Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Observe Miner
dialogues.text: (He looks exhausted.)

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: So there you are! My men and I found your clues and followed them straight here.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: We found Mao in a tent at the campsite unconscious! It seems he'll be okay. Sadly, we found no trace of the other three...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Huh? Young Kun, wh—what is...?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Nothing, pay it no mind. Those three miners are over in that cave there.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Cave? What happened!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: They're exhausted, but not in danger. Don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: R—Right, well... Thank you, all of you! I better go and see how they're doing.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: So you're taking them back to Liyue Harbor?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: That's right!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Can I come with you?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: No problem! You rescued my men. I'll be happy to assist all of you in any way I can. I'll be back soon, I need to assess their condition.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kun Jun... Oh, uh... we should be calling you Azhdaha... You're coming back to Liyue Harbor too, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Not I, merely this body.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Once I'm gone, the true owner will accompany the miners back to Liyue. Kun Jun hails from a family of famous artisans — he too will be famous in time. It would be a shame for someone of his talent to go missing.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You always did have a great admiration for blacksmiths.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Curious how swords and daggers are blind, yet their creators see so much. Perhaps empathy is mankind's proudest achievement after all?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Azhdaha. I am no longer the Geo Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: ...I can sense it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Today I am just an ordinary citizen of Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Even you met such a fate... Let's get the difficult part out of the way. I cannot guarantee that I won't be awoken a second time.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No matter. If that day comes to pass, Liyue must prepare itself to face you.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: And how will Liyue fare without Rex Lapis?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Even without a god above, this remains a nation of men. I was once their god, I ought to be here to witness their rise and fall.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: All life is shaped and then ground away by the endless flow of time. You were always the strongest among us, yet it would seem that even you have been eroded...

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: That's unimportant... fate is ordained by heaven. Even if our mission had already concluded, it would be cowardly not to strike out on the road of departure.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: You may live forever, doomed to a lonely existence... yet even this is temporary. When you reach the end of time, those people, those past and future relationships predetermined by fate... They will be waiting for you.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I do not pretend to match your rhetoric when it comes to the subject of a life long-lived. I fear that the life of an elemental being is longer than any in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Were it not so, you would have killed me long ago, and would not be having to face me again now.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You've brought a smile to my face. When all is said and done, a reunion between old friends is an auspicious occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: That day in The Chasm? Did you hesitate?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A heart of stone is a heart nonetheless. But I am the God of Contracts, and was, for a time, a god of the people of Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: You chose justice, but did not forsake your kindness. You came to me not as an assassin, and so I was willingly sealed away.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The movements of the Earth Dragon can tremble the earth and shake the heavens. With your abilities, even at my full strength, I struggled to confront you, let alone seal you away.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Hence "my" inception.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Do not forget that I was there with Liyue's founder. The face may have changed, but the content of the contract remains intact.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Old friend, God of Contracts. I hereby honor our agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Thank you, Azhdaha.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: My life is nigh on eternal. I will go on with the infinite flow of time. And you, Morax... You too will live for many a day to come.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You're leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: If it is fated, Morax... we will meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So is this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...the real Kun Jun?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Yes. Don't be alarmed, he's only asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... that was so weird. It was like he... suddenly became another person.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: In fact... we have yet to meet the real Kun Jun.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But what about Azhdaha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He was a great friend of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: He was.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Centuries may have passed since then... but events from a thousand years ago... remain crystal clear in my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A thousand years ago, Azhdaha attacked The Chasm. I tried to obstruct him, fighting him tooth and nail down the length and breadth of the mine. Finally, I brought him down, and sealed him underground.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: During that battle, Dragonfall was born. Azhdaha could sense the stone. Subconsciously, he wanted to use it to find me.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Despite being the victor, I could not claim to be stronger than he. And in his heart, he still retained an ounce of good will towards me... towards Liyue... towards life above ground.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: He was willing to be sealed away. But as the erosion set in... he forgot.

choices.text: The power of erosion is... scary.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Even I cannot avoid it. But there is something I understand better than most: When the door opens, it is time to leave.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The greater the power, the greater the danger erosion may bring about. The millennia may come and go, but even a stone may tire.

choices.text: Is that why you chose to leave...?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Personally sealing away an old friend... this is just one form of erosion I have endured.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: People abandon and surrender the things they love to pursue the right path. Perhaps this is the erosion imposed on me by the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But I was a god of mankind. My identity may change, but my eyes will bear witness to the history of humanity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You still care a lot about Liyue...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Call it... part of my duty.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I must thank you both.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No worries!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hold on.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I want to ask you something.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Oh? About what?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #About my {F#brother}{M#sister}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Paimon nearly forgot!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, not long ago we met a guy called Dain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He told us about Khaenri'ah and the punishment of the gods... That's when we realized that those events... were connected to the person we're searching for.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Zhongli, you're a god. You've lived through thousands of years of history. Surely you experienced the incident.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I cannot say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can't even give us a thread of information? This is so important to us!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I understand, but I must apologize. This is my contract.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean, another past grievance? Like the incident with Azhdaha? Too painful to talk about?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It was signed before it all began. I have always honored the contract... and kept my silence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...How can you be like that...!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: You two are friends to me. I can assure it brings me no pleasure to disappoint you. But as the God of Contracts, I cannot go back on my word.

choices.text: Well, it's not out of character.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Would you be ready to find out?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It appears your understanding of this world continues to grow.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: There are many events of ages past... many secrets that lie hidden...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: They have been eroded by time, forgotten by the people... abandoned.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But you are capable of finding them and bringing them into the light.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Those who come to witness... will witness. Those who are born to remember... will remember.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: If you take the same road as that person, there may be more difficulties ahead. But as long as you firmly believe that you are on the right path... everything has meaning.

choices.text: Is that why you chose to step down as the Geo Archon...?
Have you also been affected by erosion?

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: Ugh... Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: (He looks exhausted.)

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: Argh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did we get here? We need to go back and check on the miners!
